event_hypothesis: Prodigies were reported at Rome and terrified the citizens before the Trasimene campaign.

witnesses.quote_la: Diris tunc etiam Romani prodigiis territi sunt

notes: Orosius only; he gives a prodigy list (sun diminished, shields in the sky, two moons, bleeding ears of grain) placed immediately before Hannibal's march on Flaminius. Periocha omits the prodigies but attests the subsequent Sibylline expiation, which presupposes them.

event_hypothesis: The consul C. Flaminius set out against the auspices, ignoring adverse omens (standards stuck fast, his horse throwing him).

witnesses.quote_la: contra auspicia profectus signis militaribus effossis
Inminentes temerario duci cladem praedixerant insidentia signis examina

notes: Religious-political violation by a sitting consul. Periocha: standards dug out because they could not be pulled up, consul thrown over his horse's head; Florus adds bee swarms on the standards, eagles refusing to advance, and an earthquake during battle. Both brand Flaminius temerarius.

event_hypothesis: On news of the Trasimene disaster there was public mourning at Rome; two mothers died of joy when their sons returned unexpectedly.

witnesses.quote_la: duae matres ex iusperato receptis filiis gaudio mortuae sunt

notes: Periocha only ('Cum ad nuntium cladis Romae luctus esset...'). 'iusperato' is the source text's reading (for insperato), quoted verbatim. Public mourning, not a riot.

event_hypothesis: Because of the Trasimene defeat a ver sacrum was vowed on the authority of the Sibylline books.

witnesses.quote_la: ex Sibyllinis libris uer sacrum uotum

notes: Religious expiation decreed at Rome; periocha only, explicitly causal ('Ob hanc cladem').

event_hypothesis: Q. Fabius Maximus was appointed dictator and sent against Hannibal, adopting a strategy of avoiding battle.

witnesses.quote_la: Q. Fabius Maximus dictator aduersus Hannibalem missus
Fabii Maximi dictatoris tempus medium fuerit
Missus adversus Hannibalem postea a Romanis Q. Fabius Maximus
cognomen novum et rei publicae salutare Cunctator

notes: Divergence: periocha and Orosius give the title dictator; Eutropius says only 'missus a Romanis' and Florus gives no title, only the cognomen Cunctator and popular acclaim as 'imperii scutum'. Witnesses do not state the appointment procedure.

event_hypothesis: The master of horse M. Minucius, by denouncing the dictator as sluggish and timid, obtained by order of the people an imperium equal to the dictator's.

witnesses.quote_la: ut populi iussu aequaretur ei cum dictatore imperium

notes: Periocha only among these witnesses. Typed new-institution as an unprecedented equalization of a magister equitum with a dictator by popular enactment; could also be coded electoral-conflict (popular vote against a magistrate). Army was divided in consequence ('diuisoque exercitu').

event_hypothesis: After being rescued by Fabius, Minucius voluntarily resubmitted to the dictator, joining camps, saluting him as father, and ordering his soldiers to do the same.

witnesses.quote_la: castra cum eo iunxit et patrem eum salutauit

notes: Periocha only. Political reversal of the imperium-equalization: restoration of unified command by voluntary act, not by law.

event_hypothesis: New consuls L. Aemilius Paulus and C. Terentius Varro succeeded Fabius in the command against Hannibal.

witnesses.quote_la: Aemilio deinde Paulo et Terentio Varrone coss.
L. Aemilius Paulus P. Terentius Varro contra Hannibalem mittuntur Fabioque succedunt
L. Aemilius Paulus et P. Terentius Varro consules contra Hannibalem missi

notes: Consular succession attested by three witnesses; none of them narrates the election itself or any electoral conflict, so no electoral-conflict event is reconstructed. Eutropius and Orosius both attest discord in the field ('inpatientia Varronis consulis', Eutropius adding 'contradicente altero consule') blamed for forcing battle at Cannae; Eutropius also attests Fabius's parting admonition to the consuls. Praenomen divergence: Eutropius gives P. Terentius Varro.

event_hypothesis: After Cannae, desperate aristocrats formed a plan to abandon Italy, which P. Cornelius Scipio suppressed by forcing them at sword-point to swear not to desert the republic.

witnesses.quote_la: a nobilibus adulescentibus propter desperationem consilium de relinquenda Italia iniretur
senatores de relinquenda Italia sedibusque quaerendis consilium ineundum putarint

notes: Divergence is substantive: periocha makes the plotters 'nobiles adulescentes' confronted by Scipio as tribunus militum; Orosius makes them 'senatores', names Caecilius Metellus as instigator ('auctore Caecilio Metello'), and likewise credits Scipio tribunus militum with the sword-point oath. A sedition/defection plot suppressed; closest closed-list analogue would be riot-tumult, but no crowd violence is attested.

event_hypothesis: A state of panic and mourning gripped the city of Rome after Cannae.

witnesses.quote_la: trepidationem urbis et luctum

notes: Periocha's closing summary ('Praeterea trepidationem urbis et luctum... continet') attests urban panic as book content without narrative detail. Typed riot-tumult as nearest closed-list category; no actual rioting is attested.

event_hypothesis: Because of the shortage of soldiers, eight thousand slaves were armed and enrolled for military service.

witnesses.quote_la: Propter paucitatem militum VIII milia seruorum armata sunt
Servi, quod numquam ante, manumissi et milites facti sunt
sub titulo libertatis sacramento militiae adegit
Deerat iuventus: in sacramentum liberat servitia

notes: Typed new-institution on Eutropius's 'quod numquam ante'. Divergences: only periocha gives the figure 8,000; Eutropius and Florus say the slaves were freed/sworn in, periocha only 'armata'; Orosius specifies volunteers or slaves bought at public expense and assigns the measure to the dictator Iunius; Florus's fuller mobilization notice drifts into later years (servile troops under Gracchus).

event_hypothesis: Although there was an opportunity to ransom the prisoners taken at Cannae, the senate refused to redeem them.

witnesses.quote_la: cum potestas esset redimendi, redempti non sunt
eos cives non esse necessarios, qui cum armati essent, capi potuissent

notes: Eutropius attributes the refusal explicitly to the senate and preserves the reasoning, adding that Hannibal then executed the captives and sent three modii of gold rings to Carthage (rings also in Florus and Orosius). Periocha records only the fact of non-redemption.

event_hypothesis: The Romans appointed a dictator (Orosius: Decimus Iunius) who held an emergency levy, enrolling men from age seventeen into four legions.

witnesses.quote_la: dictatorem Decimum Iunium creant
dilectu habito ab annis decem et septem

notes: Orosius only; the periocha, Florus, and Eutropius omit this second dictatorship of the year entirely. Orosius's praenomen 'Decimus' stands alone in this input set and cannot be cross-checked within the Livian lineage.

event_hypothesis: The dictator Iunius by edict enrolled men liable for crimes or debts into the army with a promise of impunity, about six thousand men.

witnesses.quote_la: impunitate promissa militiae mancipauit

notes: Orosius only ('edicto uelut asylo patefacto... quorum numerus ad sex milia uirorum fuit'), explicitly presented as reviving an old expedient of Roman distress. Emergency levy measure; no closed-list type fits exactly.

event_hypothesis: Arms were taken down from the temples and private wealth was poured into the empty treasury to re-equip the state after Cannae.

witnesses.quote_la: Arma non erant: detracta sunt templis
egenti aerario priuatae opes refusae sunt

notes: Chronological divergence: Orosius sets both measures immediately after Cannae under the dictator Iunius; Florus attaches the mass registration of private contributions to the consulship of Laevinus and Marcellus ('Laevino Marcelloque consulibus'), i.e. apparently a later year, with senate, knights, and tribes contributing in turn. The temple-arms measure itself may belong to Book 22 or 23.

event_hypothesis: The Vestal virgins Opimia and Florentia were tried and condemned for unchastity (incestum).

witnesses.quote_la: Opimia et Florentia, uirgines Vestales, incesti damnatae sunt

notes: Periocha only among these witnesses; a religious-judicial proceeding at Rome placed after Cannae in the epitome's order.

event_hypothesis: The consul Varro was met by a crowd on his return and formally thanked for not having despaired of the republic.

witnesses.quote_la: Varroni obuiam itum et gratiae actae, quod de re p. non desperasset
Paulum puduit, Varro non desperavit

notes: Periocha gives the formal public act (obviam itum, gratiae actae); Florus preserves only the antithesis that Varro 'did not despair', without the reception scene.

event_hypothesis: In electing new consuls the younger citizens sought the advice of their elders, deferring to senior judgment in the choice of commanders.

witnesses.quote_la: iuniores a senioribus consilium de creandis consulibus petierunt

notes: Florus only, in an undated recovery passage that already includes material of later years; this electoral episode may belong to a later book rather than Book 22. Typed electoral-conflict as an irregularity of the centuriate process, though Florus presents it as concord, not conflict.
